name: Company membership
summary: How a user's home company is decided from their work-email domain, and how linked companies relate.

actions.action: Assign a user to the company
Remove a user from the company

nfr.statement: Largest companies (users, linked companies, domains) membership and lists must support.
nfr.open_question: How many users do the largest enterprise customers have today, and what is the growth target?

requirements.title: The work-email domain decides the home company
requirements.statement: A user's home company is the company matching their work-email domain. If one exists, the user joins it automatically, with no invitation or approval. If none exists, a company is created.

sources.title: Product walkthrough and clarifications recorded in the 2026-10-28 ledger

acceptance_criteria.given: Company A owns the domain acme.com
acceptance_criteria.when: A person registers and verifies jo@acme.com
acceptance_criteria.then: Their home company is A, with no company invitation or approval

acceptance_criteria.given: No company owns the domain newco.com
acceptance_criteria.when: A person registers and verifies sam@newco.com
acceptance_criteria.then: A company is created for newco.com and becomes their home company

requirements.title: Linking companies never changes a user's home company
requirements.statement: Companies can be linked to each other. A user always belongs to the company matching their domain; links give access across companies without moving the user.

sources.title: Product walkthrough and clarifications recorded in the 2026-10-28 ledger

acceptance_criteria.given: Companies A and B are linked, and a user's email is on B's domain
acceptance_criteria.when: They are added to a project owned by A
acceptance_criteria.then: Their home company is still B

requirements.title: Who Track3D's customers and users are
requirements.statement: Customers are general contractors, trade partners and owners. Users hold construction-company roles, including field engineers and superintendents.
requirements.rationale: Context for product decisions rather than a testable behaviour.

sources.title: Product walkthrough and clarifications recorded in the 2026-10-28 ledger

requirements.title: Domain and non-domain users see different features
requirements.statement: Permission visibility differs between users from the project company's domain and users from other domains. Non-domain users don't see features they can't use.
requirements.rationale: The PRD row doesn't say which features differ. Product needs to define the difference.

sources.title: Prior PRD - Roles and permissions (t3d-prd-agent prd-tech-docs)

acceptance_criteria.given: A user from a domain other than the project company's
acceptance_criteria.when: They sign in and open the project
acceptance_criteria.then: Features they have no access to are hidden
